packageRules.description: The Rust toolchain is a reviewed decision, not a dependency. `rust-toolchain.toml` is the one place it is named (ci.yml reads the channel out of that file, and the Dockerfiles' RUST_VERSION arg tracks it by hand); a bot moving any one of them alone re-introduces exactly the three-way drift OPS-4.1 closed. `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` is pinned to a `master` commit for the same reason — it has no useful release tags.

Same lockstep, from the image side: the `cargo-chef` and `rust` base tags embed the Rust minor (`latest-rust-1.94-alpine`, `1.94-bookworm`) and must not move ahead of rust-toolchain.toml. Digest updates are still wanted — they are security rebuilds of the *same* toolchain — so only the version half is disabled.

Postgres majors are not a routine bump here. The committed `.sqlx` offline query cache was verified byte-identical against the CI major (OPS-4.2), and a new major has to be re-verified the same way before the `sqlx` job's result means anything. Needs a human on the dashboard.

promtool validates the alert rules in CI and Prometheus evaluates them in the deploy overlay. If those two versions ever differ, CI is testing a different PromQL engine from the one that runs — so the ci.yml pin and the compose pin move in one pull request or not at all.
One pull request for routine Cargo churn across all three workspaces (root, web/frontend, fuzz) instead of three streams of singletons.

The Tailwind CLI and the font packages are dev-only — they produce the committed assets/main.css and ship nothing into the WASM bundle. The `css` CI job rebuilds and diffs that file, so a bad bump fails loudly rather than silently restyling the SPA.

oasdiff has no stable major tag (it is 0.x), so its pin is exact and only a bot keeps it current. Left explicitly enabled because the default 0.x handling would otherwise treat every minor as a major and park it on the dashboard.

customManagers.description: `cargo install` pins inside the Dockerfiles. These are unreviewed toolchain changes on every cache miss if left floating, so they carry exact versions — which means nothing but a bot will ever move them.
